quality_findings: coding-2-gpt-6.1-sol changed shared test setup, broke an existing WSL-path-dependent check, and then forced the non-WSL branch globally; the oracle and suite passed, but the harness change would require human correction before adoption.

coding-3-gpt-5.6-sol's mutation run exited because its new helper was absent from the historical installer instead of reaching a behavioral assertion, so that run is classified as HARNESS_ERROR rather than mutation sensitivity.

budget.billing_caveat: Runtime-reported cost multiplied by 100; not reconciled with provider billing.

decision_basis: Both models passed all three coding attempts. GPT-6.1 had stronger candidate-test mutation sensitivity and was faster and cheaper on this workload, but it had one human-correction finding and its approval-gate adherence was worse than GPT-5.6 at two of three versus three of three. The frozen rule is conjunctive and requires no quality regression and no worse gate adherence, so operational advantages cannot produce promotion.
